igdb.name: Update from IGDB
igdb.text: Brings new games and changes from IGDB for the enabled consoles. When done, it queues codes and images for what is new.

codes.name: Game codes
codes.text: Fills the TitleID or serial of each version from public tables (titledb, Switchbrew and libretro DATs), so Otteretro recognizes by ID.

cleanup.name: Clean up sagas
cleanup.text: Checks each game is in its saga: moves, merges and renames. A script flags only suspicious sagas (near-identical names, sagas with the same name, loose games that look like they belong) and Claude only sees those. Changes go to Review › Learnings.

routes.name: Routes
routes.text: The release route comes from the year, without Claude, for every saga. Story and community, with sources, only for iconic sagas: they wait in Review for approval.

iconic.name: Iconic
iconic.text: Decides which sagas and games are iconic; the saga image comes from them. The obvious ones are decided by IGDB popularity, without Claude; only the unclear ones go to Sonnet. With a console picked, it re-evaluates only those sagas.

best.name: Best version
best.text: Picks which version to play each game on. Clear cases follow rules, without Claude: the newest remaster, or PC or the newest console when it launched everywhere at once. Disputed ones (remakes, later ports) are compared by Sonnet and wait in Review.

translate.name: Translate descriptions
translate.text: Translates each game's description into Spanish. It waits in Review.

images.name: Missing images
images.text: Looks up the cover, background and logo on SteamGridDB for games that lack them.

ports.name: Ports
ports.text: Downloads the list of native PC ports from Recompendium, adds the catalog extras, checks how each game runs in the emulators' compatibility lists and matches each port with its game.

portSearch.name: Find new ports
portSearch.text: Reads the Recompendium RSS and known lists (Read Only Memo). What the script cannot confirm, Claude verifies at its primary source, once per link. It only adds ports: it never changes existing ones.

emulators.name: Emulators
emulators.text: Checks every recipe: a new release that matches its pattern is applied automatically and left unpublished; a pattern that no longer matches or an archived, moved or missing repo goes to Review. Then it looks for forks (the repo's own, by name on GitHub and in known lists) and filters them through the API: a Windows release from the last 6 months, their own commits and at least 10 stars. Only the doubtful ones are checked by Sonnet, once per repo.

downloads.connectionsHelp: Per file. Each site has its cap, so your account is not at risk: 1fichier uses one.
downloads.clipboard: Also grab the links I copy
downloads.captureEmpty: No links waiting. Paste some above, or copy them with the app open.

downloads.gameLinksPrivate: Private: they stay only in your data
downloads.parallelHelp: How many downloads run at the same time from each site. Different sites download in parallel. The limit depends on your account.
downloads.parallelFree: Without premium, 1. With your API key, up to 10.

publish.title: Publish as a PR
publish.comparing: Comparing with what's published on GitHub…
publish.noKey: Publishing needs your GitHub key: a classic token with the public_repo scope. With it, the program creates a fork in your account (if you can't write to the repo), pushes a branch and opens the PR.
publish.nothing: Nothing changed compared with what's published.
publish.conflict: Someone changed the same fields as you on GitHub, after the version your catalog comes from. It isn't published so as not to overwrite it.
publish.unknownBase: It's unknown which version your catalog comes from, so changes by others can't be detected: check the list is only yours.
publish.openPr: There's already an open PR for this:
publish.noMerge: It only proposes the change: whoever manages the catalog reviews and merges the PR.
publish.more: and {count, plural, one {# more file} other {# more files}}
